analysis_notes.summary: Torah #108 is an extremely brief moral teaching — essentially a single sentence repeated in Yiddish — warning that a momentary pleasure can cost a person both this world and the world to come. The teaching is purely cause-and-effect (eitza): brief pleasure causes catastrophic loss. There are no bechina statements anywhere in the text. No concept is declared an 'aspect of' another. Therefore no packages can be formed.
